annotations.text:
Shipping A · axis: presentation.
Why: the two tiers are the content invariant, and two equal photo cards are the only layout here that gives them equal weight; each price sits on its card head, above the body copy, in the two figures a buyer is scanning for.
Trade-off: it needs a second real photograph, so the Home Delivery card leans on our home-delivery van image; if that image is ever retired the card falls back to a second crop of the crate photo.

(Recommended) Shipping B · axis: presentation.
Why: the live section already ships a five-step flow strip under the copy, so the timeline is the treatment the page has proven; folding it into the section removes the duplicate and lands the two tiers where the strip ends, which is where a reader looking for a price arrives. It is also the shortest of the three at Tablet and second shortest at Desktop.
Trade-off: four nodes plus two end cards is more structure than two tiers strictly need, and it reads left to right, so at 390 it has to become a vertical list and gains about 470px.

Shipping C · axis: presentation.
Why: it is closest to what ships today, a photo beside the copy, so it is the cheapest to adopt, and it is the shortest artboard on this page at Desktop (724px) because the photo column absorbs the height the tier rows would otherwise add.
Trade-off: only one photo earns a place, so Home Delivery is described but never shown, and at Tablet the stack puts a 300px image above the fold before the H2 is read.
